subject: E9239F2F8F30E75D30C97D5222058E75
introduction: “All His Books will be translated. Now is the time for you to live in accordance with His words. Let your deeds be the real translation.” The guide begins there and then becomes practical: a translation never has the force of the original; it should be the work of a committee expert in both tongues; learn Persian; translate a page a day; these Tablets first, into Russian, Hindi, Esperanto; and, in a run of later letters, do not print too widely or too soon. Every scripture that has travelled has faced the same questions. The translator of Sirach apologized for his Greek; the Qur’an says each messenger speaks his people’s language; Pentecost gave every hearer his own; the King James translators called translation the opening of a window. Keats, reading Homer in Chapman’s English, is the witness for how much can cross. And Milton, who wanted Truth left free to grapple, questions the caution of the readings on publication.
questions: “Let your deeds be the real translation.” In what sense is a life a translation of a text, and what does the image ask of the reader?
The translator of Sirach says the force is lost; the King James translators say a window is opened. How do readings 4 and 5 weigh loss against access?
Why do readings 3 and 7 to 13 insist on a committee? What can several translators do that one cannot, and what might be lost?
At Pentecost the message came to each in his own tongue; the readings also urge Westerners to learn Persian. Are these two movements in tension?
Milton trusted truth “in a free and open encounter”. What reasons do readings 45 to 52 give for restraint, and are they reasons of principle or of the moment?

outside.why: “All His Books will be translated. Now is the time for you to live in accordance with His words.” Be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only.
Let deeds be the translation. Ye are our epistle written in our hearts, known and read of all men.
A Tablet is to be translated by a committee of Persians and English-speakers together. In the multitude of counsellors there is safety.
A translation “is not as effective as the original”. The grandson who put Sirach into Greek: the same things uttered in Hebrew, and translated into another tongue, have not the same force in them.

The King James translators argued the other side to their readers in 1611: translation it is that openeth the window, to let in the light; that breaketh the shell, that we may eat the kernel. Is a translation a loss, a window, or both?

However eloquent the translation, the original has “a different splendor”. Keats could not read Greek; Chapman’s English Homer made him feel like some watcher of the skies when a new planet swims into his ken. How much can come across?

The Faith had not taken hold in Paris, and translation is among the reasons considered. The Qur’an: We never sent a messenger save with the language of his folk, that he might make the message clear for them.
A committee of those who have mastered the languages. Two are better than one; for if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow.

The most difficult texts need the most able committee. In Nehemiah a company of Levites stands with Ezra: they read in the book distinctly, and gave the sense, and caused them to understand the reading.

“Nothing has been translated well”, for individuals did it. Paul: there are so many kinds of voices in the world; if I know not the meaning of the voice, I shall be unto him that speaketh a barbarian.
Translate a page every day to gain skill. Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings.

“Study Persian.” At Pentecost the hearers do not have to learn a language: every man heard them speak in his own. Which is the more natural movement for a scripture, toward its readers’ tongues or theirs toward its own?
Learn the tongue “so as to learn of the meanings of the divine words”. Understandest thou what thou readest?
What is needed is eloquence and fluency in the language of the hearers. Except ye utter by the tongue words easy to be understood, how shall it be known what is spoken?
A prayer that the translator be “a sign of fluency”. My tongue is the pen of a ready writer.
“You are the first person who translated” some of these words. Every scribe instructed unto the kingdom brings forth out of his treasure things new and old.
Translate, “so that the people of the West may become informed”. How shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard?
The Tablets of counsel should be translated first. I had rather speak five words with my understanding, that I might teach others also, than ten thousand words in an unknown tongue.
Hindi, Gujarati, Russian, Danish, German. A great multitude of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues.
The Hidden Words in Esperanto. Then will I turn to the people a pure language, that they may all call upon the name of the Lord, to serve him with one consent.
The hope of a common auxiliary tongue. Babel is the story it answers: let us go down, and there confound their language, that they may not understand one another’s speech.
Friends printing and translating to spread the message. How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that bringeth good tidings.
When the Qur’an was printed, its pages wrapped medicines in shops. Give not that which is holy unto the dogs, neither cast ye your pearls before swine.

Wide publication is called unwise. Milton, against all restraint of printing: let Truth and Falsehood grapple; who ever knew Truth put to the worse, in a free and open encounter? What does the reading fear that Milton did not?
Publishing now “would slacken the people’s thirst”; first souls must be prepared. I have fed you with milk, and not with meat: for hitherto ye were not able to bear it.
The Bayán’s laws have been superseded, and its publication is not pressed. The law was our schoolmaster; after that faith is come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster.
Print only if wisdom permits, and with the sovereign’s leave. Be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves.
“The time has not yet arrived” to spread the Tablets with full freedom. I have yet many things to say unto you, but ye cannot bear them now.
The Teachings have spread and translations can be had. Go ye therefore, and teach all nations.

shortfall: Many readings are short practical notes about particular translations, translators and printings in various languages; they were given companions where they state a principle (committee work, the original’s force, timing, discretion) and otherwise left alone.

kjv-translators-openeth-the-window.text: Translation it is that openeth the window, to let in the light; that breaketh the shell, that we may eat the kernel; that putteth aside the curtain, that we may look into the most holy place; that removeth the cover of the well, that we may come by the water
